composers_checked.name: Hummel, Johann Nepomuk
composers_checked.note: All 20 IMSLP pages judged; gap check against the Wikipedia list and the MusicBrainz release list; recordings via Apple Music and MusicBrainz (Naxos Music Library and Presto not used); RECHECK 2026-10-17: S.30, Op. 2a No. 1 and Op. 111a searched again (Deezer, Apple, MusicBrainz, web): still no usable recording

note: Reicha and Hummel complete: 51 IMSLP pages judged; gap check against the Wikipedia work lists (after Stone/Grove, Sachs/Zimmerschied) and the full MusicBrainz release lists of both composers. Floor evidence is Apple Music plus MusicBrainz releases (the Apple US catalogue lacks several discs found on MusicBrainz, e.g. Sony SK 53118, Alpha 369, Quatuor Ardeo, MDG 311 0380). The Naxos Music Library (login) and Presto (blocks scripts) were not used, so pages skipped as "not performed or recorded" (Reicha Op. 49 Nos. 2-3, Op. 52, Op. 58, Op. 90 Nos. 1 and 3-6, Op. 95 Nos. 2-3, Op. 98 Nos. 1-5, Op. 92 Nos. 2-3, Op. 47; Hummel S.30, Op. 2a No. 1) have no recording on either service and may deserve a second look. REICHA: single works of multi-work pages are kept only where recorded. Gap works without an IMSLP page: Op. 94 No. 3 (Quatuor Ardeo), Op. 51 variations, Grand Trio in G, String Trio in F, and two E-flat quintets with viola (Wikipedia lists one as [No. 4]; recordings number them 1 and 2). The Kreutzer Quartet cycle on Toccata has Vols. 1-2 only (Op. 48, Op. 49 No. 1). Grande symphonie de salon No. 2 has ten players (out of scope); the glass-harmonica quintet (c. 1806) was not found recorded. HUMMEL: the piano trios are numbered 1-7 on Naxos, Chandos, harmonia mundi and MusicBrainz (Op. 12 = No. 1 ... Op. 96 = No. 7) but differently on IMSLP and Wikipedia, so titles carry opus numbers only and the recordings' numbering is in aka. Op. 74 and Op. 114 have piano-quintet arrangements by the composer (IMSLP: Artaria, Haslinger); only Op. 74's is recorded (Atalanta Fugiens, Nepomuk Fortepiano Quintet) and is kept as a gap entry on the Septet page. Serenades Op. 63/66: I count five players (the Paris print's viola replaces the guitar); IMSLP's tags for Op. 66 list six, so please check. Hummel's chamber arrangements of Mozart concertos and symphonies and of Beethoven symphonies (S. 131-156) are arrangements of other composers' works and out. Levels and popularity are estimates. RECHECK 2026-10-17: 3 works added (Reicha, Flute Quartets Op. 98 Nos. 1-3: Hünteler, R. and J. Kussmaul, Dieltiens, MDG, 1996; Deezer 157083122, AllMusic; the first pass missed this disc); 15 lines settled as not performed or recorded after fresh Deezer, Apple (composerTerm and title searches), MusicBrainz and web searches (30 works; the Op. 98 line now covers Nos. 4-5 only); 0 still not checked; hand edits: the Op. 98 skipped line retitled '(Nos. 4-5)' with works set to 2, evidence rewritten on the other 14 lines, composers_checked Reicha kept 31->34 and skipped 50->47, year left blank on the three new entries to match No. 6 (IMSLP: 1822 or earlier, Wikipedia: before 1815). Op. 98 keys per IMSLP: Book I E minor, A major, D major; Book II G minor, C major, G major (a retailer's Bärenreiter listing of Nos. 4-6 repeats Book I's keys). MusicBrainz files Reicha as 'Antoine Reicha' (a quoted 'Anton Reicha' search returns nothing). Hummel S.30: the only recording is the computer-made 'Electronic Hummel, Vol. 1' (Al Goranski, 2023), which does not meet the floor. Hummel Op. 63/66: the Deezer album 'Hummel: Serenades, Op. 53, 63 & 66' (157108822) titles both Grande Serenades 'for Piano, Violin, Guitar, Clarinet and Bassoon', which supports the five-player count for Op. 66 asked about above. Reicha's glass-harmonica quintet (c. 1806, Wikipedia list) searched again on Deezer and MusicBrainz: still not found recorded.
